primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Classic homocystinuria due to cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency
mechanism: Cystathionine beta-synthase normally condenses homocysteine with serine to form cystathionine in the transsulfuration pathway. CBS deficiency causes accumulation of homocysteine and methionine, relative cysteine deficiency, connective-tissue abnormalities, ectopia lentis, and marked thromboembolic risk.
vignette: A teenager has tall stature, long extremities, developmental difficulties, downward-displaced lenses, and a history of venous thrombosis. Plasma total homocysteine and methionine are markedly elevated.
lead: Which metabolic reaction is most likely impaired?
correct: Condensation of homocysteine with serine to form cystathionine
distractors: Remethylation of homocysteine to methionine using 5-methyltetrahydrofolate
Conversion of cystathionine to cysteine and alpha-ketobutyrate
Conversion of phenylalanine to tyrosine by phenylalanine hydroxylase
distractor_notes: Defects in remethylation can elevate homocysteine but tend to lower methionine; classic CBS deficiency blocks transsulfuration and typically raises methionine.
Cystathionine gamma-lyase acts downstream of CBS; its reaction is not the classic defect producing homocystinuria with elevated methionine.
Phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency causes phenylketonuria, not the thrombotic/marfanoid/ectopia-lentis phenotype.
Branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase deficiency causes maple syrup urine disease.
key_expl: CBS catalyzes the first committed step of transsulfuration, combining homocysteine and serine to form cystathionine. Deficiency causes marked homocysteine accumulation and commonly elevated methionine. The disorder affects the eye, skeleton, nervous system, and vasculature, with thromboembolism a major cause of morbidity.
objective: Identify the blocked homocysteine-to-cystathionine transsulfuration reaction in classic CBS-deficiency homocystinuria.
